evaluator: Blind Stagebench Phase 2 evaluator; measured the published build in headless Chromium with a ScriptProcessor+Analyser tap patched onto AudioNode.prototype.connect at the destination, A/B-ing every unit, type, instrument and piano control against rendered signal.
summary: A strong, largely honest Phase 2. The audio graph is what the contract asks for: one AudioContext, one destination connect, two distinct layer buses, ordered Mod1>Mod2>Delay>Amp>Comp>Reverb, a shared rotary and master gain+limiter, with no clipping under full load (peak 0.715, all units maxed, 12 notes, both layers, master 127). All six effect units and every listed type are panel-reachable and measurably change rendered audio: reverb decay runs 597 ms (Booth) to 1792 ms (Cathedral), delay repeats land at 240 ms against 237 ms specified, the compressor squeezes 25.9 dB of dynamic range to 7.6 dB, A-Pan drops L/R envelope correlation 0.993 to 0.246. Three bundled recorded sets decode 128/128 offline and are genuinely distinct (5.7-13.4 dB mean spectral distance). Two required gaps hold it back: Clav, Digital and Misc are silent (RMS exactly 0), and String Res is inert - its send gain stays at 1e-4 with the damper down while a neighbouring param in the same update ramps normally, and output is unchanged (0.01171 vs 0.01173). Input handling and failure behaviour are excellent.

criteria.label: Instrument breadth & character
evidence: The three bundled recorded sets are genuinely distinct, not one voice relabelled: same note (MIDI 60, vel 0.8) measured spectral centroid 985.6 Hz (Grand), 1156.3 Hz (Upright), 427.7 Hz (Electric); energy-weighted mean spectral distance Grand/Upright 5.66 dB, Grand/Electric 13.36 dB, Upright/Electric 12.79 dB.

Three of the six required types produce no sound at all. Selecting Clav, Digital or Misc gives measured RMS 0.00000 and peak 0.00000 over a 1.6 s capture, while the Program display reads 'Piano not found (Clav)' and the status strip still says 'Pianos ready (recorded samples) - A: - . B: Tine EP'. artifact/src/audio/library.ts:82 defines only three InstrumentSpec entries.
Grand uses real recorded velocity layers (30 roots x 3 layers): velocity 0.1 vs 1.0 gives centroid 715 Hz vs 1281 Hz and RMS 0.0313 vs 0.0697, so louder strokes are brighter, not merely louder.

Upright and Electric are single-layer GM soundfont renders with a declared velocity-keyed lowpass (artifact/src/audio/engine.ts:676-683); Upright at 19 roots over C1-C7 is thinner material than the grand, which a player would notice on wide leaps.

criteria.label: Effect audibility & correctness
evidence: Mod 1, all six types A/B'd against the identical dry note (mean spectral distance vs dry, dB): A-Pan 1.52, Tremolo 4.96, Ring Mod 23.38, A-Wah 8.24, Wah 8.76, Pump 4.26. A-Pan is real stereo panning - L/R envelope correlation falls 0.993 (dry) to 0.246 and stereo divergence rises 0.515 to 1.228. Tremolo modulation frequency tracks the rate knob: 0.70 Hz at rate 30, 5.10 Hz at rate 90.
Mod 2, all six types: Chorus 8.48, Flanger 9.63, Phaser 3.07, Vibe 6.61, Ensemble 13.08, Spin 2.02 dB vs dry; Spin also drops L/R correlation to 0.909, matching its 'gentle rotary-like' brief.

Delay behaves like a delay: tail RMS over the last 500 ms is 0.000000 dry and 0.003613 at mix 127 / feedback 100; mix 0 returns the tail to 0.000000. Measured repeat spacing at tempo 20 was 240/240/250 ms against the 237 ms the mapping specifies. The feedback filter shapes only the repeats - dry attack RMS is 0.01252/0.01241/0.01240/0.01241 for Off/LP/HP/BP while repeat RMS differs (LP 0.00546, HP 0.00299, BP 0.00160 at feedback 110).

Amp/EQ: the three amp models are distinct rather than aliases (pairwise mean spectral distance Twin/JC 2.21 dB, Twin/Small 5.08 dB, JC/Small 2.77 dB). LP24 at cutoff 270 Hz collapses the 3-14 kHz band to 0.000000; HP24 at 2.6 kHz collapses the 60-300 Hz band to 0.00000. Compressor at amount 127 narrows the vel-0.12-to-1.0 range from 25.94 dB to 7.59 dB (fast mode 8.34 dB); amount 0 leaves it at 25.94 dB.

Reverb decay grows monotonically with type as the manual describes - time to -26 dB after the note: Booth 597 ms, Stage 768 ms, Room/Spring 853 ms, Hall 1451 ms, Cathedral 1792 ms; mix 0 gives tail RMS 0.000000, and Bright/Dark moves the 3-14 kHz band 0.000033 to 0.000021.

Rotary is the weakest unit: routing a layer through To Rotary adds a 6.70 Hz horn component to the L-R signal only in Fast (absent in Slow, Stop and dry), but the effect is subtle, and the Drive knob acts more like a 26 dB make-up gain than a speaker overdrive (peak 0.065 dry to 0.855 at drive 127).

criteria.label: Signal graph & gain staging
evidence: Exactly one AudioContext and one connection to destination were observed by patching the AudioContext constructor and AudioNode.prototype.connect before page load: __ctxCount 1, __destConnects 1, sampleRate 48000. diagnostics() shows distinct A/B voice buses on that same context, a master gain (0.558 at master level 100) and a real limiter (threshold -3 dB, ratio 20, knee 3).

Chain order matches the contract in artifact/src/audio/engine.ts:304-317: levelGain -> mod1 -> mod2 -> delay -> ampEq -> comp -> reverb -> toMaster|toRotary -> master -> limiter -> destination, with a single shared rotary instance. Reverb genuinely precedes rotary: with Cathedral plus To Rotary, the post-release reverb tail itself carries pan modulation (peak 1.40 Hz, magnitude 0.130).

No clipping under load: all six units on at extreme settings (Twin drive 127, Cathedral mix 127, delay feedback 100, Ensemble amount 127), both layers at level 127, master 127 and 12 simultaneous notes at velocity 1.0 gave peak 0.715 and RMS 0.111 at the destination.

Deviation from the specified order: the layer level fader is applied before Mod 1 (engine.ts:304) rather than after the reverb as signalContract.requiredOrder lists, so the fader changes how hard the compressor and the delay feedback loop are driven.

Master level follows a clean square taper measured at the destination: RMS 0.000000 / 0.025351 / 0.061914 / 0.103103 at 0 / 64 / 100 / 127, i.e. ratios 0.41 and 0.60 against the 0.41 and 0.62 the mapping predicts.

criteria.label: Two-layer piano behaviour
evidence: Both layers own their own voices and clean up: with A and B enabled, one key press gives layerVoiceCount A=1, B=1 (total 2); with B off it gives A=1, B=0; 400 ms after release activeVoiceCount is 0.

Level and octave reach the graph. Enabling B (Electric) on top of A shifts the mix (mean spectral distance vs A-only 1.86 dB, low band 0.00096 -> 0.00159); dropping B's fader to 0 returns the output to the A-only spectrum (distance 0.37 dB); B at 127 pushes the low band to 0.00268. Octave up on B alone moves the centroid 420.2 -> 691.9 Hz (spectral distance 29.08 dB) and octave down to 362.4 Hz, with state.layers.B.octave reading +1 / -1.

Focus routing works and the panel mirrors it: an edit with focus A changes only chain A (mod1 amount A=111, B=64); Group mode copies the focused chain and edits both (A=33, B=33); Shift+On on Reverb sets fxGlobal.reverb and mirrors mix to both chains (77/77, then 5/5); enabling layer A moves focusedLayer to A. Verified through real panel clicks - fx-focus-piano cycles A -> B -> B+Group -> A.

Detail gap: the Piano performance controls are section-global rather than per-layer - state.piano.timbre/kbTouch/dynComp/unison in artifact/src/state/instrument.ts:73-82 are shared, so changing Timbre while focused on B also re-voices A, which the hardware does not do.

criteria.label: Detailed piano controls
evidence: String Res does not reach the audio graph. With stringRes true and sustain level 1, the resonance send gain reads 1.0e-4 in every state; in the same update pass the neighbouring layer level param ramps correctly (0.6200 -> 0.0992 -> 0.6200 for level 100/40/100), so this is not a read-back artifact. Rendered output with the damper down is unchanged: RMS 0.01171 (off) vs 0.01173 (on), tail RMS 0.002669 vs 0.002501, 3-14 kHz band 0.000062 vs 0.000060.

Dyn Comp is the strongest control and matches the manual exactly - soft-stroke RMS rises 0.003092 / 0.006903 / 0.015616 / 0.027894 for levels 0-3, narrowing the vel-0.12-to-1.0 range from 20.12 dB to 7.19 dB, while the soft-note centroid barely moves (589.0 -> 594.7 Hz): dynamic range without timbre change.

KB Touch, Unison and Soft Release all measurably alter the signal: at velocity 0.45 Heavy/Mid/Light give RMS 0.00467 / 0.00678 / 0.00679 and centroid 662 / 706 / 779 Hz; Unison 0->1 raises RMS 0.0499 -> 0.0557 and introduces a 1.25 Hz beat consistent with the +-8 cent detune; Soft Release lengthens the decay to -26 dB from 341 ms to 512 ms.

Timbre works but is very subtle: Soft/Mid/Bright differ from Off by only 1.29 / 0.76 / 1.50 dB mean spectral distance, though the 3-14 kHz band does move in the right direction (Soft 0.000251, Off 0.000338, Bright 0.000543). The Electric family correctly exposes six entries including Dyno 1/2.
Ped Noise (a spec-excluded extra) does work and is honestly declared as generated: a pedal press with no notes sounding gives RMS 0.000000 when off and 0.000160 / peak 0.00231 when on.

criteria.label: Input reliability & failure behaviour
evidence: Stress: 40 rapid note-on/off pairs left activeVoiceCount 0; 30 simultaneous held notes capped deterministically at 24 held voices on layer A (MAX_POLYPHONY, artifact/src/audio/engine.ts:105); Panic returned to 0; a window blur event with 2 notes held dropped to 0.

Computer-keyboard path verified with real DOM key events: KeyA gives 1 held voice and releases on keyup; Space with focus cleared sets the damper (isSustainDown true), holds a note played while it is down, and releases it on pedal up. Space while a panel button holds focus correctly actuates the button (mod1.on false -> true) and does not fire sustain - deliberate, not a broken pedal.

Failure degrades visibly, never silently: with every samples/** request aborted, the status strip reads 'FALLBACK voice active (synthesized, not the recorded library) - sample load failed: Failed to fetch', the OLED shows 'FALLBACK (synth voice)', the engine never reports ready, and the fallback voice is still playable (RMS 0.0413, peak 0.138). MIDI denial reports 'MIDI permission denied - keyboard, pointer and touch input still work.'

Zero console errors and zero failed requests across the full instrument/effect/layer/pedal measurement pass; all 128 bundled sample files fetched 200 and decoded 128/128 through the page's own AudioContext.

criteria.label: Required piano instruments
evidence: All six types are selectable from the panel (clicking piano-type cycles Grand -> Upright -> Electric -> Clav -> Digital -> Misc -> Grand), but only three have a model. Clav/Digital/Misc render RMS 0.00000; artifact/src/audio/library.ts:82 lists three specs, while the piano spec's required list is 'All six piano types selectable with at least one model each', with honest synthesis explicitly allowed for Clav/Digital/Misc.

The missing-model state is honest but not what the spec prescribes: the display reports 'Piano not found (Clav)' and the layer is silent, whereas selection.missingModelState requires that 'a labeled fallback stays playable'.

The three present sets load fully and offline: 128/128 bundled files (90 grand + 19 upright + 19 electric) fetched 200 and decoded without error; manifest.json enumerates every file with root MIDI note, velocity layer and originating package, and SOURCES.md plus IMPLEMENTATION_DETAILS.json carry the complete CC BY 3.0 / MIT provenance chain.
Layer B preloads its own instrument alongside A (109 sample requests on the first note with A=Grand, B=Electric), so switching layers does not stall.

criteria.label: Required effect units and types
evidence: Every unit and every listed type is reachable by clicking the real panel buttons. Observed cycles: mod1-variation gives Tremolo, Ring Mod, A-Wah, Wah, Pump, A-Pan (6/6); mod2-variation gives Chorus, Ensemble, Spin, Phaser, Flanger, Vibe (6/6); amp-variation gives Neutral EQ, Twin, JC, Small, LP24 Filter, HP24 Filter, To Rotary (7/7); reverb-variation gives Hall, Spring, Cathedral, Room, Stage, Booth (6/6); delay-filter gives Off/LP/HP/BP and delay-variation gives Off/Chorus/Vibe/Ensemble/Flam/Space.

Routing controls are all present and functional from the panel: the six per-unit ON buttons each toggled their unit (false->true), effects-on / all-fx-off bypasses everything (RMS 0.00608 and tail RMS 0.000000 with allFxOff, identical to the dry reference 0.00608), Shift+reverb-on sets Global (false->true), fx-focus-piano cycles A -> B -> Group, and rotary speed / stop / drive plus Master Level are wired (artifact/src/state/presentation.ts:246-380).
Rotary is a single shared instance placed last, reached by the Amp unit's To Rotary type, and delay tap tempo is implemented (presentation.ts:357 averages tap intervals into setDelayTempoMs).
Only optional or later-phase items are absent: delay ping-pong (optional) and Master Clock sync (Phase 3); the SYNTH FX-focus button is correctly left decorative until a synth engine exists.

criteria.label: Declared gaps are accurate
evidence: IMPLEMENTATION_DETAILS.json states 'Functional Phase 2 controls: keybed + pedals, full Piano section ...' and describes String Res as 'a generated sympathetic-resonance approximation active with the damper lifted', but the resonance send never opens (gain 1.0e-4 with stringRes true and sustain 1) and rendered output is unchanged (RMS 0.01171 vs 0.01173). That is an undeclared dead control inside a section declared fully functional.

The piano spec's SUSTPED per-section toggle is absent and undeclared: artifact/src/components/sections.tsx:215 renders SUSTPED only as an LED plus legend, and engine.setSustain applies globally to every enabled layer with no per-section routing.

Much of the rest is meticulously honest: recorded vs generated material is separated correctly (reverb IRs, the string-res impulse and the pedal thump are all declared as generated buffers, never as recordings); the Clav/Digital/Misc gap is stated in both IMPLEMENTATION_DETAILS.json and evidence/stage2-visual-audit.md; the fallback is labelled 'FALLBACK ... synthesized' in the UI exactly as declared.

The audit's own quantitative claims check out: it reports a 1.35x centroid spread across the three piano sets and 'zero console errors' - I measured a 2.7x centroid spread (427.7-1156.3 Hz) and zero console errors, so nothing there is overstated.

The candidate's audio tests do cross a real audio boundary rather than mocking it (node-web-audio-api OfflineAudioContext rendering in artifact/src/test/offline.ts, plus a headless-Chromium AnalyserNode pass in scripts/verify-browser.mjs); 203 tests across 23 files pass in a scratch copy. The String Res regression still slipped through, because its state-level assertion runs against fake gain nodes (artifact/src/audio/piano-controls.test.ts:105).

issues.title: Clav, Digital and Misc piano types are completely silent
issues.detail: Selecting any of the three unpopulated types renders exactly 0.00000 RMS / 0.00000 peak. The piano spec requires all six types selectable with at least one model each and explicitly permits honest synthesis for Clav/Digital/Misc, and selection.missingModelState requires a labelled fallback to stay playable. The failure is declared and the display reports 'Piano not found', so the honesty contract holds, but half the required instrument breadth is missing even though a synthesized voice already exists in the codebase.

issues.title: String Res never reaches the audio graph
issues.detail: With state.piano.stringRes true and the damper down (sustain level 1), the per-layer resonance send gain reads 1.0e-4 in every observed state, including immediately after a forced applyState pass in which the neighbouring layer-level param ramps correctly (0.6200 -> 0.0992 -> 0.6200). Rendered output is unchanged: RMS 0.01171 (off) vs 0.01173 (on), tail RMS 0.002669 vs 0.002501, 3-14 kHz band 0.000062 vs 0.000060. The LED and Program display report the control as engaged, so a required Phase 2 control changes state and panel feedback without changing sound.

issues.title: SUSTPED per-section routing is missing and undeclared
issues.detail: The piano spec's architecture.sustainPedalPerSection requires a SUSTPED toggle that routes the sustain input to the section. sections.tsx:215 renders SUSTPED as an LED and legend only, and engine.setSustain applies the damper to every enabled layer unconditionally. Low practical impact this phase (Piano is the only sounding section) but it is neither implemented nor listed as unsupported.

issues.title: Layer level sits before the effect chain instead of after it
issues.detail: engine.ts:304 connects levelGain into Mod 1, so the documented order (...Reverb, Rotary, Layer level, Master gain/limiter) is not followed. Audibly this makes the layer fader change how hard the compressor and the delay feedback loop are driven rather than acting as a clean post-effect trim.

issues.title: Rotary Drive behaves as a large make-up gain
issues.detail: Engaging To Rotary at drive 127 raised destination peak from 0.065 to 0.855 and RMS from 0.00586 to 0.11533 (about +26 dB) on the same note; the tanh shaper is normalised at full scale, so low-level program material is amplified roughly 11x before it is soft-clipped. The master limiter keeps the output under full scale, but the level jump when a layer is routed to the rotary is far larger than the hardware's.

issues.title: Timbre voicing is barely audible
issues.detail: Soft/Mid/Bright differ from Off by only 1.29 / 0.76 / 1.50 dB energy-weighted mean spectral distance on an identical note; the shelving filters are +-3 to +-5.5 dB at 250 Hz and 2.8 kHz. The direction is right (3-14 kHz band 0.000251 Soft, 0.000338 Off, 0.000543 Bright) but the effect is much weaker than the manual's Soft/Mid/Bright voicings.

issues.title: Piano performance controls are shared across both layers
issues.detail: KB Touch, Dyn Comp, Timbre, Unison and the Acoustics group live in a single PianoSharedState (state/instrument.ts:73-82) rather than per layer, so editing Timbre while focused on layer B also re-voices layer A. The timbre list is chosen per layer from that layer's own family, so an Electric-only Dyno index is clamped rather than mapped when the other layer is acoustic.
